Proper scoring rules for predictive distributions

Source: R/scoring.R
scoring_rule.Rd

Scores each observation under the fitted predictive distribution (Gneiting and Raftery 2007). Smaller is better for every rule.

  • "log": negative log predictive density or mass.

  • "crps": continuous ranked probability score int (F(z) - 1(y <= z))^2 dz, by quadrature for continuous laws and by summation for counts.

  • "dss": Dawid-Sebastiani score (y - m)^2 / v + log v.

  • "brier" and "rps": Brier and ranked probability scores for ordinal and nominal families (summed over the classes). For bernoulli and binomial families "brier" is the usual (y / size - p)^2 with p the predicted success probability.

Usage

scoring_rule(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  rule = c("log", "crps", "dss", "brier", "rps"),
  re = c("conditional", "zero", "marginal"),
  nmarginal = 200,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted model.

newdata

Optional data frame with the response; defaults to the fitting data.

rule

Scoring rule.

re

Random effects used for prediction, as in predict(): "conditional" uses the estimated effects of known groups, "zero" sets them to zero, and "marginal" scores the predictive law of a new group: the mixture over nmarginal draws of the random effects from their estimated distribution (for each observation; the dependence between observations of one group is not used).

nmarginal

Number of random effect draws for re = "marginal".

seed

Optional seed for the random effect draws.

Value

Numeric vector of scores, one per observation.

Details

For Bayesian fits every rule scores the posterior predictive distribution, the mixture of the laws of the posterior draws (at most 1000, evenly thinned): the log score uses the mean density, the CRPS the mean CDF, the Dawid-Sebastiani score the total predictive mean and variance, and the Brier and ranked probability scores the mean class probabilities. The CRPS is infinite when the predictive law has no finite mean; a quadrature that does not converge raises regcomp_numerical_failure.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100)); d$y <- rnorm(100, 1 + d$x)
fit <- regcomp(y ~ x, family = "normal", data = d)
mean(scoring_rule(fit, rule = "crps"))
#> [1] 0.539673
